source_title: Hyundai BAYON Variants: HX 2 to HX 10 Explained - hyundai.com
source_excerpt:
Choosing the right SUV becomes easier when you know which features each variant offers. The Hyundai BAYON comes in seven trims, from the HX 2 to the top-end HX 10, with differences in comfort, infotainment, transmission and driver-assistance technology. Whether you want essential safety features, the convenience of an automatic transmission or advanced features such as SmartSense Level 2 Pro ADAS, this guide breaks down the Hyundai BAYON variants to help you find the one that best suits your needs and budget.
What Variants Does the Hyundai BAYON Come In?
The Hyundai BAYON comes in seven variants, each adding equipment over the one below while sharing the same 1.5-litre petrol engine. The BAYON car variants run HX 2, HX 3 and HX 3+ at the accessible end, HX 5 and HX 6 in the mid-range, and HX 8 and HX 10 at the top.
What Engine and Transmission Do Hyundai BAYON Variants Offer?
All seven Hyundai BAYON variants use the same 1.5-litre MPi petrol engine, producing 115 PS of power and 144 Nm of torque. The main difference lies in the transmission options available across the range. Buyers can choose a manual gearbox for greater control over gear changes or an automatic option for added convenience in everyday driving.
The 6-speed manual transmission is available across all variants, starting with the HX 2. It allows drivers to control gear changes based on road conditions and driving preferences. This option may suit those who prefer a more involved driving experience or want to keep the purchase cost lower than that of an automatic variant.
The Intelligent Variable Transmission (iVT) is available from the HX 5 onwards. Unlike a conventional gearbox with fixed gear ratios, it adjusts its ratio as driving conditions change. This helps deliver smooth acceleration without the need for manual gear changes, making it convenient for daily commutes and stop-and-go city traffic. The iVT variants also offer paddle shifters and drive mode selection, giving drivers more control over how the car responds. The 6-speed manual may be a suitable choice if you prefer direct control over gear changes, while the iVT is worth considering if you spend considerable time driving in traffic and want a clutch-free experience.
What Does Each Hyundai BAYON Variant Add?
Each trim builds on the one below, so the right one depends on the features you value most.
The HX 2 is the entry trim, with six airbags, ESC, ABS with EBD, rear parking sensors and a highline TPMS as standard, plus LED projector headlamps, R16 steel wheels, manual air-conditioning and rear AC vents. It covers the essentials at the lowest entry point.
The HX 3 adds a reversing camera, a smart key with push-button start and a 26.03 cm (10.25-inch) touchscreen with wireless Android Auto and Apple CarPlay, for buyers who want connected infotainment over the base trim.
The HX 3+ adds an electric sunroof, roof rails and R17-style steel wheels, for buyers who want a sunroof and a sportier stance on a budget.
The HX 5 introduces the iVT automatic option, plus automatic headlamps, fully automatic climate control, Hyundai Bluelink connected car technology, over-the-air updates, a wireless charger and cruise control, for buyers who want everyday comfort and an automatic.
The HX 6 steps up with dual LED projector headlamps, a panoramic sunroof, R17 diamond-cut alloy wheels, a leather-wrapped steering wheel and gear knob and ambient lighting, for buyers who want a more premium cabin.
The HX 8 adds front and side parking sensors, a Surround View Monitor, a dashcam, rear disc brakes, leatherette seats, an electric 8-way driver seat and ventilated front seats, for buyers wanting near-top comfort.
The HX 10 is the top BAYON variant, adding the full SmartSense Level 2 Pro ADAS suite with a Blind-spot View Monitor, a 12.3-inch ccNC navigation screen and digital cluster, a Generative AI voice assistant, Bose audio and dual curved panoramic displays, for buyers who want every feature the BAYON offers.

How many variants does the Hyundai BAYON have?
The Hyundai BAYON comes in seven variants: HX 2, HX 3, HX 3+, HX 5, HX 6, HX 8 and HX 10, all with a 1.5-litre petrol engine.
Which Hyundai BAYON variants have an automatic?
The iVT automatic is available from the HX 5 variant upward, covering the HX 5, HX 6, HX 8 and HX 10.
Which Hyundai BAYON variant has a sunroof?
The HX 3+ and HX 5 have an electric sunroof, while the HX 6, HX 8 and HX 10 feature a larger panoramic sunroof.
The top HX 10 variant carries the full Hyundai SmartSense Level 2 Pro ADAS suite, with the Surround View Monitor also featuring on the HX 8.
